big: Meena sold one share at a ₹50,000 profit and another at a ₹30,000 loss. She expected tax on ₹50,000. The law lets her net the two, so only ₹20,000 is taxed.

lines: I lost money on a share. Is that loss just gone?
No. In the same year it can cut your gains. If it is not used, it can be carried to later years, but only if you file your return on time.

rows: Carry forward, if the return is filed on time
note: A long-term capital loss can usually be set off only against long-term gains. A short-term loss can be set off against both, subject to the rules.

title: Losses and advance tax
stops: A loss can reduce a gain in the same year
A loss can be carried forward without filing a return
Advance tax is paid in instalments during the year
Selling at a loss just for tax is always wise
caps: Set-off reduces the gain that is taxed.
Carry forward needs the return filed by the due date.
Advance tax falls due in instalments on set dates during the year.
Do not let the tax tail wag the investing dog, so keep the plan in view.

q: Rohan has a ₹40,000 gain on one fund and a ₹10,000 loss on another, same type, same year. What is taxed?
why: The loss is set off against the gain, leaving ₹30,000 to tax.
₹40,000 ignores the loss, which the law allows him to set off.
₹50,000 adds the loss to the gain, which reverses the idea.
₹10,000 is only the loss, and not what is left after setting it off.

q: Meena has a loss she cannot use this year. What must she do to carry it forward?
opts: Tell her broker in a letter
File her return by the due date
Wait five years and then claim
why: A letter to a broker has no effect on tax records.
No extra payment is needed to carry a loss forward.
Carry forward of such losses usually needs a return filed on time.
Waiting does not help. The loss must be reported each year.

q: Rohan sells a fund at a loss only to cut tax, and then wants to invest again for the same goal. What should he keep in mind?
opts: That losses are always a good thing
That he must never hold the fund again
That tax rules do not apply to him
Costs and his plan, not just the tax
why: A loss is not good in itself. It only offsets a gain.
No rule forbids holding it again, but the plan should lead.
Tax rules apply to every taxpayer, whatever the case.
Selling has costs and may break his plan.

q: Dadi expects large capital gains this year. What does advance tax ask of her?
opts: Pay everything on the last day of the year
Pay tax in instalments during the year
Pay only when the tax office sends a letter
why: Paying everything at the end can mean interest for delay.
Above a set limit, tax is paid in instalments in the year.
Waiting for a letter is not how advance tax works.
Retirement does not pause the tax on her gains.

pts: A loss can cut a gain in the same year. This is called set-off.
To carry a loss forward, file the return by the due date.
Advance tax is paid in instalments. Do not sell only for tax.
